note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypertension and palpitations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old male with longstanding hypertension since young age presenting for management. Patient reports emergency room visit in March for elevated blood pressure and palpitations, which he attributes to consuming several cups of coffee without breakfast and possible panic attack. Denies recurrence of palpitations since that time. Recently started on new antihypertensive regimen by new primary care physician approximately one month ago. Reports checking blood pressure daily at home with readings consistently in the 146-155 mmHg range. Attempting to reduce salt intake. Exercises on treadmill when able. Strong family history of hypertension.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current palpitations. Denies chest pain, dyspnea, or other cardiac symptoms. No reports of edema noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension since young age.

MEDICATIONS
1. Benicar HCT (olmesartan/hydrochlorothiazide) 40-25 mg daily
2. Amlodipine 10 mg daily
3. Spironolactone (newly initiated at this visit)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant family history of hypertension in multiple family members.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with girlfriend. Exercises on treadmill when possible. Attempting to reduce dietary salt intake.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing male, alert and oriented.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, heart sounds normal.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no masses palpated.
Extremities: No edema noted in ankles or feet.

RESULTS
Potassium level one week ago: 4.0 mEq/L (normal).
Thyroid profile from March 1, 2021 copied forward per request.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
49-year-old male with resistant hypertension on three antihypertensive medications at maximum doses with inadequate blood pressure control. Currently on amlodipine 10 mg daily and Benicar HCT 40-25 mg daily. Discussed resistant hypertension and likely secondary causes including possible hyperaldosteronism. Initiated spironolactone for additional blood pressure reduction. Discussed dietary modifications including DASH diet plan, salt restriction to 1500-2000 mg daily, and increased physical activity targeting 30 minutes most days. Provided patient with heart.org resources and DASH diet information. Counseled on potential side effects of spironolactone including dizziness, electrolyte disturbances (hyperkalemia and hyponatremia), gynecomastia (rare), and need for hydration. Recheck metabolic panel and blood pressure in two weeks. If inadequate response to spironolactone, next options include carvedilol or referral to resistant hypertension clinic for evaluation of secondary causes and consideration of interventional procedures such as renal denervation.
